grh_290cab48c8205f8ebae8.title: Spring In The Air
paragraphs: With spring putting romance in the air, Judy Price confides to Dr. Christian that she is secretly engaged to young physician Ralph Gardner. Ralph is building his career with financial help from a disapproving uncle and has insisted that nobody know about the engagement until he is established. When he learns Judy has told Christian, he becomes angry, tells her to pretend they have broken up and stops seeing her openly. Judy believes he is working nights as hard as she is so they can marry sooner. Christian finally persuades the exhausted Judy to go out for dinner, where they unexpectedly find Ralph dancing with wealthy Laura Payson. Confronted outside, Ralph makes his choice plain: he intends to marry Laura and resents Judy questioning him. Judy is devastated, but Christian helps her see that losing a man willing to trade loyalty for money and position is not the end of love. He reminds her that, like spring itself, love can come around again.

grh_294eaeb7c5f05b724e3a.title: One Way Passage
paragraphs: Escaped convict Dan Hardesty, being returned to San Quentin to face execution, meets terminally ill Joan Ames aboard a Pacific liner. Neither initially reveals the death sentence hanging over them, and they fall in love while trying to crowd a lifetime of happiness into the voyage and a day ashore in Honolulu. At San Francisco Joan discovers Dan is the prisoner, runs after him for one final goodbye and dies as he is taken toward the death house. On New Year's Eve in Acapulco, their doctor watches two cocktail glasses mysteriously break with their stems crossed in the X Dan and Joan used to mark their happiest moments, suggesting they have found each other after death.

grh_294bef67e7cc8dd77ce6.title: All My Sons
paragraphs: Manufacturer Joe Keller has built his life around providing for his family, but his son Chris discovers that Joe knowingly allowed defective aircraft cylinders to be shipped during the war and let partner Herbert Deever take the blame. Twenty-one pilots died, and Joe insists he did it to protect the business for his sons. A letter from missing son Larry reveals that Larry learned of his father's crime and deliberately went to his death because he could not live with the shame. Joe finally understands that the dead airmen were 'all my sons' too. Moments later a gunshot from the house tells Chris that his father has killed himself.
